transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?
My mind feels foggy all the time—I can’t focus at work or even finish a simple puzzle like I used to. It's starting to really affect my daily life, so I thought I should get it checked out.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood, such as feeling sad, empty, or hopeless, along with this foggy feeling and difficulty focusing?

Yeah, I've been carrying around this heavy, empty sort of sadness lately, like I'm just going through the motions at home and at work. Sometimes I even catch myself tearing up for no real reason when I'm alone in the break room or driving home in the morning.
Do you often find yourself feeling guilty about things that have happened in the past or worrying that you're to blame for things that aren't going well?

It's not really about things from the distant past, but I definitely feel like I'm messing everything up lately with my job and my family. It gets to the point where I sometimes catch myself thinking everyone might just be better off without me around.
Have you lost interest in activities or hobbies that you normally enjoy, or do you still find some pleasure in doing things you've always liked?

Yes, I've completely lost interest in things I used to love, like cooking dinner with my wife or playing guitar with my kid. Now, even on my nights off, I just sit on the couch staring at the TV and turn them down when they ask me to join in because I just don't feel like doing anything.
How long have you been experiencing these feelings of sadness, emptiness, and loss of interest in activities, was it a gradual change or did it start suddenly?

These feelings have been going on for about three weeks now. While I had some ongoing stress with my schedule and family before, this sudden shift of feeling empty and losing interest really hit me during a particularly busy, stressful month at the casino when the tension with my wife flared up.
Have you experienced episodes like this before in your life, or is this the first time you've felt this way for an extended period?
No, this is the first time I've ever felt this way. I've had stressful times in the past, but this heavy sadness and brain fog are completely new to me.
You mentioned these feelings started about three weeks ago, can you tell me more about what was happening in the days or week leading up to when you first noticed this change in your mood and focus?

In the weeks leading up to this, I was dealing with a very busy month of rotating night shifts at the casino, which was already exhausting. On top of that, my wife and I had a major argument about whether to move closer to my in-laws for childcare support, causing ongoing tension that left me feeling emotionally checked out. That stress seemed to boil over right before this heavy fog and sadness fully set in.

You've mentioned that these feelings have been going on for about three weeks, can you tell me if there have been any days during this time where you felt somewhat better or if the feelings of sadness and emptiness have been constant?

No, there haven't really been any better days; the heavy, empty sadness has been constant over the last three weeks. Every single day, I feel like I'm just constantly going through the motions at home and at work. It doesn't seem to lift at all.
Have you experienced any days during these three weeks where you felt nearly back to your normal self, even if just for a brief period, or has the sadness and emptiness been unremitting?

No, I haven't had any days where I felt back to my normal self. This heavy, empty feeling has been completely unremitting and drags me down day after day without any break. It's just been a constant weight every single day.

Can you tell me if there have been any periods, even brief, where you've felt a significant improvement in your mood or a return of interest in activities during these three weeks, or has the low mood and lack of interest been persistent without any notable improvements?

No, there haven't been any improvements or breaks at all. The low mood and lack of interest have been completely persistent day in and day out over the whole three weeks. I haven't had a single moment where I suddenly felt better or wanted to do any of the things I used to enjoy.

You've mentioned that your symptoms have been constant for three weeks without any improvement, but can you tell me if you've had at least two weeks where you felt the symptoms nearly every day, or have there been any fluctuations?

Yes, I have felt these symptoms nearly every single day, all day long, for the entire three weeks since this started. There haven't been any fluctuations or days where the cloud lifted even a little bit. It has just been a constant, daily struggle without any breaks.

You've had these symptoms for three weeks without any improvement, but can you confirm if you've had at least two weeks where these feelings of sadness, emptiness, and loss of interest were present for most of every day, helping me understand the consistency of your experience?

Yes, I can definitely confirm that. For the entire three weeks, these feelings of sadness, emptiness, and having no interest in anything have been there almost every single day, all day long. It has been a constant daily struggle with absolutely no relief or better days.

You've described a constant feeling of sadness and emptiness for three weeks without any relief, can you confirm if these symptoms have been present for at least two weeks, and if they have been severe enough to interfere with your daily life nearly every day during this period?

Yes, they have been completely constant for the last three weeks without any breaks, and they are definitely interfering with my daily life. At work, my supervisor has already pulled me aside twice for missing things on the security monitors because I'm so slowed down. At home, my wife is really upset with me because I'm just emotionally checked out and not engaging with her or our kid at all.
To confirm, you've experienced these depressive symptoms for three weeks straight without any day where you felt significantly better, is that correct?

Yes, that is correct. It has been a solid three weeks without a single day of feeling better or getting any relief. It all started right when things got extremely busy at the casino and the tension with my wife flared up.

Just to make sure I understand, you're saying that for the entire three weeks, you've had no days where you felt even slightly better, and these symptoms of sadness, emptiness, and lack of interest have been present every single day without any letup?

Yes, that’s exactly right. For the whole three weeks, there hasn't been a single good day or even a brief break from how I feel. The heavy sadness and complete lack of interest have been a constant, daily presence, leaving me feeling entirely checked out every single day.

You've confirmed that your symptoms have been constant for three weeks without any improvement, but can you specify if you've had any periods, even brief, where you've felt some return of your normal energy or motivation, helping me understand the severity of your experience?

No, I haven't had any periods of normal energy or motivation at all during these past three weeks. This heavy, foggy feeling has been completely constant without any real breaks. I just feel drained and slowed down every single day.

You've described a consistent experience of depressive symptoms over the past three weeks without any relief. Can you tell me if you've had any thoughts of self-harm or suicide during this period, as this would be an important factor in understanding the severity of your condition?

I don’t have any active plan to hurt myself, but I do get these passive thoughts sometimes. When I’m driving home after a long shift, I catch myself thinking it wouldn’t really matter if I didn’t wake up or if something happened to me. It just feels like my family might be better off without me messing everything up.
Can you tell me more about these passive thoughts, how often they occur, and if they've been getting stronger or weaker over the past three weeks?

These thoughts usually happen a few times a week, especially when I'm driving home exhausted after a long night shift. They've stayed pretty consistent over the past three weeks as the strain on my marriage and job has intensified. I don't have any plan to act on them, but the feeling that everyone would be better off without me just keeps creeping in when I'm at my lowest.

You've been experiencing these depressive symptoms for three weeks without any relief, but can you tell me if you've noticed any difference in the severity of your symptoms from one week to the next, or have they remained about the same?
I haven't really noticed any change in how bad it is from week to week. The symptoms have felt pretty much the same—consistently heavy and foggy—ever since they started about three weeks ago.
Have you experienced any increase in the frequency or intensity of these passive thoughts about not being around, or have they remained relatively consistent over the past three weeks?
I'm not quite sure if they've actually changed in intensity or frequency. They have just been happening on and off since all of this started, without any clear pattern of getting worse or better.
Have you experienced any increase in the frequency or intensity of these passive thoughts about not being around, or have they remained relatively consistent over the past three weeks?

They've remained relatively consistent over the past three weeks. They mostly happen when I'm driving home tired after a long shift, thinking it might be easier if I just didn't wake up, but I don't have any active plans to hurt myself.

Given that your symptoms have been constant for three weeks, can you confirm if you've had at least five of the depressive symptoms we've discussed nearly every day, such as feelings of sadness, emptiness, loss of interest, changes in appetite or sleep, fatigue, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, difficulty concentrating, and recurrent thoughts of death, for the majority of the days during this period?

Yes, I can confirm that. Almost all of those feelings—the constant empty sadness, having no interest in family time, not wanting to eat, feeling physically slowed down, the severe brain fog, and those dark thoughts—have been happening nearly every single day without any real break. It's just been a constant, exhausting struggle for the past three weeks.

You've described a range of depressive symptoms that have been constant for three weeks, but can you tell me if you feel like you're able to function and carry out your daily responsibilities, albeit with difficulty, or if these symptoms are so severe that they're significantly impairing your ability to work, take care of yourself, and engage with your family?

They are definitely causing a major strain and significantly impairing my life. At work, my supervisor has already pulled me aside twice for missing things on the security monitors because of my fogginess. At home, my wife is really upset because I'm completely checked out and not engaging with her or our child at all.
